Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Hertz Energy Inc. (CSE: HZ) (OTCQB: HZLIF) (FSE: A340) ("Hertz" or the "Company") announces that it has amended the terms of its non-brokered private placement previously announced on October 9, 2026 (the "Offering").

As originally announced, the Offering was to consist of up to 1,664,150 charity flow-through units at a price of $0.265 per unit, up to 1,665,600 charity flow-through units at a price of $0.25 per unit and up to 4,166,666 non-flow-through units at a price of $0.18 per unit, for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $1,607,400. The Company has replaced the charity flow-through units with critical minerals flow-through units and traditional flow-through units, and has reduced the size of the non-flow-through portion of the Offering, as described below. Coloured Ties Capital Inc., whose participation in the Offering was announced on October 15, 2026, will not be participating in the amended Offering.

Amended Offering

The Offering, as amended, will consist of:

CRITICAL MINERALS FLOW-THROUGH UNITS

  1. up to 2,500,000 critical minerals flow-through units of the Company (each, a "Lake George FT Unit") at a price of $0.18 per Lake George FT Unit for gross proceeds of up to $450,000;

TRADITIONAL FLOW-THROUGH UNITS

  1. up to 2,000,000 traditional flow-through units of the Company (each, a "Craig FT Unit" and, together with the Lake George FT Units, the "FT Units") at a price of $0.16 per Craig FT Unit for gross proceeds of up to $320,000; and

HARD DOLLAR UNITS

  1. up to 3,000,000 units of the Company (each, an "HD Unit") at a price of $0.18 per HD Unit for gross proceeds of up to $540,000,

for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $1,310,000.

Each FT Unit will consist of one common share of the Company that will qualify as a "flow-through share" (an "FT Share") within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (the "Income Tax Act") and one common share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"). Each HD Unit will consist of one common share of the Company (a "Share") and one Warrant.

Each Warrant will entitle the holder to purchase one common share of the Company (a "Warrant Share") at a price of $0.30 per Warrant Share at any time for a period of 24 months from the closing date of the Offering (the "Closing Date"), subject to the following acceleration right. If, at any time after the date that is four months and one day after the Closing Date, the closing price of the common shares on the CSE is at or above $0.50 per share for 7 consecutive trading days (the "Triggering Event"), the Company may, at any time after the Triggering Event, accelerate the expiry date of the Warrants by giving ten calendar days' notice to the holders of the Warrants by way of news release, and in such case the Warrants will expire on the first day that is 30 calendar days after the date on which such notice is given.

Use of Proceeds

The gross proceeds from the sale of Lake George FT Units will be used for exploration at the Company's Lake George antimony-tungsten project in New Brunswick, and the gross proceeds from the sale of Craig FT Units will be used for exploration at the Company's Craig silver project in Yukon. The net proceeds from the sale of HD Units will be used for general working capital and administrative purposes.

The gross proceeds from the sale of Lake George FT Units will be used to incur, on or before December 31, 2027, resource exploration expenses that will constitute "Canadian exploration expenses" as defined in subsection 66.1(6) of the Income Tax Act and "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" as defined in subsection 127(9) of the Income Tax Act. The gross proceeds from the sale of Craig FT Units will be used to incur, on or before December 31, 2027, resource exploration expenses that will constitute "Canadian exploration expenses" as defined in subsection 66.1(6) of the Income Tax Act and "flow-through mining expenditures" as defined in subsection 127(9) of the Income Tax Act (collectively with the foregoing, the "Qualifying Expenditures"). The Qualifying Expenditures will be renounced on a pro rata basis to each subscriber for FT Units with an effective date of no later than December 31, 2026, in accordance with the Income Tax Act.

Closing and Conditions

The Offering is expected to close on or before December 11, 2026, or such other date as the Company may determine, and may close in one or more tranches. Completion of the Offering is subject to certain conditions, including receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including the final approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE").

The Company may pay finder's fees in connection with the Offering in accordance with the policies of the CSE, which may include the payment of cash and/or the issuance of warrants.

All securities issued under the Offering, including any Warrant Shares issued on exercise of the Warrants, will be subject to a statutory hold period expiring four months and one day from the Closing Date.

This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any securities. Any public offering of securities in the United States must be made by means of a prospectus containing detailed information about the Company and management, as well as financial statements. "United States" and "U.S. person" have the respective meanings assigned in Regulation S under the U.S. Securities Act.

About Hertz Energy Inc.

Hertz Energy is a British Columbia-based junior exploration company focused on the exploration of its Lake George Antimony and Tungsten Project, which is adjacent to the Lake George Antimony Mine, which has been tendered by the Province of New Brunswick to Agnico Eagle's Critical Minerals Division, Avenir Minerals. Additionally, Hertz is exploring its Craig Silver Project in the Yukon, which has a small indicated high grade mineral resource and has been underexplored. Hertz also owns the Agastya Lithium Project in Quebec, located amidst Lift Power's Adina and Galine lithium projects.

ATLANTA & ZUG, Switzerland--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Coca-Cola Company and Gutsche Family Investments (GFI) have completed the sale of a 75% controlling interest in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa Pty. Ltd. (CCBA) to Coca-Cola HBC AG.

The proposed transaction was first announced in October 2025. The companies closed on Nov. 27 after receiving all necessary regulatory approvals in Africa.

Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola HBC have a separate option agreement providing Coca-Cola HBC the opportunity to acquire the remaining 25% stake in CCBA held by Coca-Cola within a six-year period.

CCBA is the largest Coca-Cola bottler in Africa, operating in 14 countries. Following completion of the deal, Coca-Cola HBC is the second-largest Coca-Cola bottler globally by volume, extending its footprint to 43 markets and serving approximately 1.2 billion consumers across Europe and Africa.

Advancing Coca-Cola's Refranchising Strategy

The completion of the transaction marks another significant milestone in Coca-Cola's ongoing strategy to refranchise company-owned and controlled bottling operations.

“This transaction reflects the strength of the Coca-Cola system and our long-term commitment to building locally led, world-class bottling operations,” said Henrique Braun, CEO of The Coca-Cola Company. “CCBA has established a strong foundation across Africa, and Coca-Cola HBC brings proven capabilities, deep market expertise and a successful track record of investing for sustainable growth.”

Luis Felipe Avellar, president of the Africa operating unit of The Coca Cola Company, said, “We are confident this combination will create new opportunities for customers, consumers and communities across the continent. Coca-Cola HBC is a strong, valued partner that has the ability to grow our business in Africa.”

The Gutsche family will remain connected to the Coca-Cola system and Africa through its ownership stake in Coca-Cola HBC.

Strengthening Coca-Cola HBC’s Presence in Africa

The acquisition builds on Coca-Cola HBC’s origins in Nigeria 75 years ago and its expansion into Egypt in 2022. Following completion of the acquisition, Coca-Cola HBC now represents approximately two-thirds of Africa’s total Coca-Cola system volume and serves more than half of the continent’s population. The combination creates a stronger platform to share capabilities, invest in people and infrastructure, and drive sustainable, profitable growth.

Zoran Bogdanovic, CEO of Coca-Cola HBC, said: “Today we mark a historic milestone as we complete the acquisition of CCBA. Africa is where Coca-Cola HBC began 75 years ago, and this acquisition significantly strengthens our presence across this incredible continent, creating a strong platform for sustainable, profitable growth. Our listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange this week further underlines our long-term commitment to South Africa and the broader African continent.

“CCBA is a high-quality business with strong market positions, deep local knowledge and talented people. We are very pleased to welcome our new colleagues to Coca-Cola HBC. Together, we will invest in our leading 24/7 portfolio, our bespoke capabilities and our passionate people to capture the significant opportunities ahead.

“I would like to thank The Coca-Cola Company and the Gutsche family for their trust and partnership, and our teams across CCBA, Coca-Cola HBC and the wider Coca-Cola system for their commitment in completing this transaction. We look forward to working together to drive joint success.”

As part of the transaction, Coca-Cola sold 41.52% of its 66.52% stake in CCBA to Coca-Cola HBC, while Coca-Cola HBC acquired the 33.48% stake held by GFI.

Rothschild & Co. acted as sole financial adviser to Coca-Cola. Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, Amsterdam Branch and UBS AG London Branch acted as financial advisers to Coca-Cola HBC. Nomura International acted as sole financial adviser to GFI.

About The Coca-Cola Company

The Coca-Cola Company (NYSE: KO) is a total beverage company with products sold in more than 200 countries and territories. Our company’s purpose is to refresh the world and make a difference. We sell multiple billion-dollar brands across several beverage categories worldwide. Our portfolio of sparkling soft drink brands includes Coca-Cola, Sprite and Fanta. Our water, sports, coffee and tea brands include Dasani, smartwater, vitaminwater, Topo Chico, BODYARMOR, Powerade, Costa, Georgia, Fuze Tea, Gold Peak and Ayataka. Our juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverage brands include Minute Maid, Simply, innocent, Del Valle, fairlife and Santa Clara. We’re constantly transforming our portfolio, from reducing sugar in our drinks to bringing innovative new products to market. We seek to positively impact people’s lives, communities and the planet through water replenishment, packaging recycling, sustainable sourcing practices and carbon emissions reductions across our value chain. Together with our bottling partners, we employ more than 700,000 people, helping bring economic opportunity to local communities worldwide. Learn more at www.coca-colacompany.com and follow us on Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn.

About Coca-Cola HBC AG

Coca-Cola HBC is a growth-focused consumer packaged goods business and strategic bottling partner of The Coca-Cola Company. Our business was founded in Nigeria in 1951, and this year we celebrate our 75th anniversary. We open up moments that refresh us all, by creating value for our stakeholders and supporting the socio-economic development of the communities in which we operate. With a vision to be the leading 24/7 beverage partner, we offer drinks for all occasions around the clock. Following the completion of our acquisition of a majority stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa on 27 November 2026, we work together with our customers to serve more than 1.2 billion consumers across 43 markets in Europe and Africa.

Our portfolio is one of the strongest, broadest and most flexible in the beverage industry, with consumer-leading brands across the sparkling, adult sparkling, juice, water, sport, energy, ready-to-drink tea, coffee, and premium spirits categories, with snacks as an additional offering. Our products include Coca-Cola, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, Fanta, Sprite, Schweppes, Kinley, Costa Coffee, Caffè Vergnano, Valser, Romerquelle, Dasani and other water brands, FuzeTea, Powerade, Cappy, Monster Energy, Finlandia Vodka, The Macallan, Jack Daniel's and Plazma. We foster an open and inclusive work environment for approximately 50,000 employees and believe that a positive environmental impact is integral to our future growth. We are among the leaders of the global beverage industry across major sustainability benchmarks, including the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Indices, CDP, MSCI ESG, FTSE ESG and ISS ESG.

Coca-Cola HBC is listed on the London Stock Exchange (LSE: CCH), Euronext Athens (Euronext Athens: EEE) and the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE: CHB). For more information, please visit https://www.coca-colahellenic.com

Today, November 27, 2026: Hotel101 Global signs definitive binding agreements for the development of Hotel101-Hyderabad, India

Hotel101-Hyderabad is set to have approx. 625 rooms occupying the top 7 floors of The Harvest Building in Kokapet, Hyderabad’s premium neighborhood in Hyderabad’s western corridor near the Financial District and HITEC City

Hotel101-Hyderabad is expected to have a project value of approx. ₹5.95 billion (US$64.4 million)

Hyderabad is often referred to as India’s tech capital and is one of its fastest-growing technology and business hubs, with major IT companies such as Microsoft, Amazon, and Infosys contributing to demand for quality accommodations.

Some of the branded hotels currently operating near Kokapet and the Financial District include the Hyatt, Sheraton, Fairfield by Marriott and Westin.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hotel101 Global Holdings Corp. (NASDAQ Ticker: HBNB) (“Hotel101” or “Hotel101 Global”), a leading asset-light, prop-tech hospitality platform pioneering a globally standardized “condotel” business model, listed on the Nasdaq Stock Exchange and a subsidiary of Philippine-listed DoubleDragon Corporation (PSE Ticker: DD), announces the signing of definitive binding agreements for the joint venture development of an approx. 625-room Hotel101 in Kokapet, Hyderabad, India. This expansion marks a significant milestone in the company's global growth strategy, bringing its novel, globally standardized “condotel” business model to one of India’s fastest-growing technology and business hubs.

The joint venture partner for Hotel101-Hyderabad is Pooja Crafted Homes (“PCH”), a Hyderabad-based developer founded in 2001 that has developed residential and commercial projects totaling more than 5.5 million square feet. Introduced and facilitated by CBRE India, the partnership pairs PCH’s local development experience with Hotel101 Global’s platform. PCH is also developing one of Hyderabad’s first luxury mixed-use developments that may include a JW Marriott-branded hotel and branded residences.

Hotel101 Global Team believes it ensures all its projects via direct developments, joint ventures and licensing to local developers in various countries worldwide are in prime and strategic locations.

Hotel101-Hyderabad is planned to occupy the top 7 floors of The Harvest Building, a premium Grade-A commercial development in Kokapet. This strategic high-rise positioning is expected to offer guests breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding landscape, including Kokapet Lake and the vibrant western corridor skyline. Kokapet has rapidly emerged as one of Hyderabad’s premier luxury and investment destinations, known for its modern infrastructure, upscale developments, and seamless blend of residential, commercial, and recreational spaces.

Key Location Advantages:

  • Prime Western Corridor Position: Located in Kokapet, directly adjacent to the Financial District and just minutes from Gachibowli and HITEC City. Upon completion, guests are expected to benefit from excellent connectivity via the Outer Ring Road (“ORR”), upcoming metro expansions, and proximity to major IT hubs housing global companies like Microsoft, Amazon, and Infosys.
  • Proximity to Business and Employment Hubs: Ideal for business travelers and corporate guests, with immediate access to Hyderabad’s booming Financial District, IT parks, and commercial centers. Hotel101 Global believes the area’s strong job market and high demand for quality accommodation drive consistent occupancy potential.
  • Lifestyle and Leisure Appeal: Surrounded by modern amenities including premium malls (such as Kokapet One), restaurants, green spaces, and natural attractions like Khajaguda Hills. The location is expected to offer the balance of urban convenience and serene surroundings, providing leisure travelers with easy access to Hyderabad’s renowned heritage sites, including Charminar and Golconda Fort, along with its dynamic cultural attractions.
  • Investment and Growth Potential: Kokapet is one of Hyderabad’s most active real estate markets, benefiting from gated communities, world-class infrastructure, high rental demand, and strong appreciation driven by IT sector growth and premium developments.

When completed, Hotel101-Hyderabad is expected to have a project value of approx. ₹5.95 billion (US$64.4 million) and is expected to be the largest hotel by room count in Hyderabad, India, forming part of Hotel101 Global’s global expansion strategy.

Hotel101-Hyderabad is expected to offer 4-star amenities at affordable prices, featuring breathtaking views from its elevated floors, swimming pools, all-day dining, a modern fitness center, function rooms, a business center, a convenience store, and approx. 625 signature HappyRooms. Consistent with Hotel101’s offerings across its locations globally, guests are expected to enjoy modern, tech-enabled rooms, 24/7 reception, and a range of lifestyle amenities tailored for both business and leisure travelers.

The development forms part of Hotel101 Global’s global expansion strategy through joint ventures with local partners and is subject to customary governmental, regulatory, corporate and other approvals.

About Hotel101 Global

Listed on Nasdaq (Ticker: HBNB) with a market capitalization of approx. US$1 billion as of November 26, 2026, Hotel101 is an asset-light, prop-tech hospitality platform pioneering a globally standardized “condotel” business model. Hotel101 aims to disrupt the global hotel and hospitality sector through its unique tech-enabled business model that positions it to generate revenues twice: first from the advance sale of individual hotel units during the construction phase; and second, from long-term recurring revenue derived from day-to-day hotel operations. The expansion of Hotel101 toward its long-term goal to operate in 100 countries globally is expected to be driven mainly by joint ventures and, in the future, license agreements with local developers in various countries worldwide.

The Hotel101 Global Group is advancing its global expansion plans toward its medium-term goal to be in 25 countries and its long-term goal of operating one million Hotel101 rooms in 100 countries globally.

TAICHUNG, Taiwan, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd (NASDAQ: AGCC) ("Agencia" or the "Company") today provided an update on its AI computing and data center business and reaffirmed its commitment to compliance with the applicable laws and regulations governing its business. The Company also clarified certain matters referred to in a media report published on November 25, 2026 (the "Report"). The Report does not allege that the Company has breached any law or regulation.

Expanding From Whisky Into AI Computing Infrastructure and Data Center Operations

Agencia listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market in October 2025 as an importer and distributor of whisky, a business that it continues to operate. In reviewing opportunities for growth beyond whisky, the Board of Directors identified strong demand for AI computing capacity and data centers in Southeast Asia, a region in which the Company and its management have established business relationships. Southeast Asia has attracted substantial data center investment from international operators, supported by the availability of land and power at competitive cost. The Company believes that this market offers long-term growth opportunities.

To develop that opportunity, the Board appointed Mr. Li Qiang as Chairman on December 11, 2025. Mr. Li has more than 20 years of experience in the data center and technology infrastructure industry, and he oversees the development of the Company's data center business.

Since announcing its AI computing strategy in February 2026, Agencia has been developing its data center and AI computing business and, directly or through its subsidiaries, has entered into a number of agreements for that purpose, as disclosed in its reports filed with or furnished to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"). The Company expects to begin providing AI computing services once the computing capacity it has contracted from its provider is in place, subject to and in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

Like other companies listed in the United States, Agencia aims to build long-term value for its shareholders, and it will continue to evaluate opportunities that can do so within applicable laws and regulations.

Commitment to Compliance

Agencia is committed to conducting its business in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, including the export control laws and regulations of the United States. The Company has not sold or supplied any product or service to any party in breach of the export control laws of the United States or of any other jurisdiction, and it has no intention of doing so.

Under the Company's computing capacity agreement, the provider warrants that the equipment used to provide the services is sourced through authorized sales channels and is exported and imported in compliance with applicable export control laws.

On November 19, 2026, the Bureau of Industry and Security of the U.S. Department of Commerce ("BIS") published an interim final rule on remote access to advanced semiconductors. The rule introduces new requirements that may apply to the Company's computing capacity and customer arrangements. Those requirements, and the steps that manufacturers and suppliers are taking in response to them, may affect those arrangements, including their timing. The Company is reviewing the rule, and its supplier and customer arrangements, with its advisers. It is committed to complying with all applicable rules and regulations and will provide services only as they permit.

Clarification Regarding Recent Media Report

The Company wishes to clarify two matters referred to in the Report.

The Company's business. The Company is not a seller or reseller of semiconductor chips or hardware. Agencia's data center business is a services business comprising two service lines: data center colocation services, which will provide space, power and connectivity for customers’ own equipment, and AI computing services, in which the Company contracts for computing capacity to provide AI computing cloud services to its customers. No AI semiconductors, hardware or servers are, or are planned to be, sold, delivered or transferred to any customer in either service line.

Relevant entities highlighted in the Report. The Report describes Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings Limited ("Yuxing InfoTech") as the parent company of Ricloud AI Inc. ("Ricloud AI"). The document that the Report cites for that statement, the 2025 annual report of Yuxing InfoTech, lists Ricloud Corp. as a subsidiary of Yuxing InfoTech. It does not list Ricloud AI as a subsidiary. Ricloud Corp. and Ricloud AI are separate legal entities.

The Company's related party relationships and transactions are disclosed in its filings with the SEC, including its prospectus filed on July 20, 2026. Mr. Li's positions with Yuxing InfoTech and with Ricloud AI are described in that prospectus.

"Agencia began as a small whisky business, and we are building a second business in data center and AI computing infrastructure because we see a real opportunity to create value for our shareholders," said Mr. LIU Shihao, Chief Financial Officer of Agencia. "Our focus is on disciplined execution and on building this business transparently and in compliance with the laws of the United States and of every country in which we operate." 

About Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd

Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd is a Nasdaq-listed company with two principal business focuses: (i) its established premium whisky operations; and (ii) the development of data center and AI computing infrastructure, including data center colocation services and cloud-based AI computing services.

Since early 2026, the Company has launched and been developing its AI Computing Infrastructure Initiative, covering data center colocation and AI cloud computing services through subsidiaries in Singapore, Indonesia and other jurisdictions. This initiative represents a principal business focus, backed by substantive contractual arrangements for commercial AI computing cloud services and the development of supporting data center, power, network and technical infrastructure. The Company’s historical operating revenue has been derived from its whisky operations, and the data center and AI computing business remain in development and deployment and is subject to significant business, financing, construction, technology, regulatory, customer demand and execution risks.

  • In a world-first, XPENG’s humanoid robot IRON hosted an automotive press conference, announcing the establishment of XPENG’s Hong Kong R&D Centre, dedicated to humanoid robotics and general-purpose intelligence. IRON is set to begin its international deployment in the second half of 2027.
  • XPENG is on track to surpass 100,000 annual overseas vehicle sales for the first time in 2026 and aims to more than double its overseas sales in 2027.
  • XPENG plans to introduce five new models across overseas markets in 2027, including the New P7, which will launch in Europe, its first overseas market, in the second quarter of 2027. The next wave of expansion begins with the L05’s launch in Thailand in December 2026.
  • XPENG plans to deploy four X-Energy megawatt charging stations across three continents within three months, accelerating the global expansion of its charging infrastructure.
  • XPENG plans to begin the overseas rollout of its advanced driver-assistance system in the first half of 2027, with a global launch of its Robotaxi targeted for 2027.

GUANGZHOU, China, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XPENG today unveiled the next phase of its global Physical AI strategy at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show, outlining its 2027 expansion roadmap across AI vehicles, humanoid robotics and autonomous mobility. Key plans include the introduction of five new vehicle models across international markets, with Europe confirmed as the first overseas market for the New P7, alongside the planned overseas deployment of its humanoid robot IRON and the international introduction of its Robotaxi programme.

XPENG also announced the establishment of its Hong Kong R&D Centre, the company’s ninth R&D centre worldwide, alongside plans to expand its X-Energy megawatt charging infrastructure across three continents.

Building on XPENG AI Day 2026 earlier in the week, the exhibition brought together international media and partners to experience how XPENG is translating its Physical AI innovations into real-world applications.


XPENG showcases its latest innovations in Physical AI at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.

IRON Takes the Mic: From Stage to Showroom

At the Guangzhou Auto Show, IRON took centre stage to host XPENG’s press conference, introducing its capabilities and interacting with an international audience. Beyond the stage, multiple IRON humanoid robots took on customer-facing roles together for the first time, serving as sales assistants, receptionists and technology guides across XPENG’s exhibition booth. They welcomed visitors, introduced vehicles and answered product enquiries, demonstrating their potential for real-world retail applications.

During the press conference, IRON also announced the official establishment of XPENG’s Hong Kong R&D Centre, which will focus on humanoid robotics and general-purpose intelligence. Its key research areas include whole-body motion control, mobile manipulation, world models and embodied intelligence. Research will also span advanced algorithms, AI software and system architecture, and data engineering. Leveraging Hong Kong’s strong research ecosystem and technology talent, the new centre will further strengthen XPENG’s global R&D capabilities in Physical AI.


XPENG’s humanoid robots IRON demonstrate their service capabilities, welcoming visitors and introducing vehicles at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.

After eight years of research and development, IRON is moving beyond technology demonstrations towards real-world service applications. In the first quarter of 2027, IRON will begin its first showroom assignments at XPENG retail locations in China, gaining practical experience in everyday retail environments. In the second half of 2027, XPENG plans to extend IRON’s deployment internationally, starting with its overseas showroom network.

“The true value of Physical AI lies not in what technology can demonstrate on stage, but in what it can deliver in the real world,” said He Xiaopeng, Chairman and CEO of XPENG. “IRON’s transition from research and development to everyday service environments represents an important step in this journey. We believe the next wave of AI innovation will increasingly take place in the physical world, transforming how people move, work and interact with technology. In 2027, we plan to accelerate the global deployment of our AI vehicles, humanoid robots and Robotaxis, turning technological innovation into tangible value for customers around the world.”


He Xiaopeng, Chairman and CEO of XPENG, joins humanoid robot IRON on stage at XPENG’s press conference at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.

XPENG Accelerates Global Vehicle Expansion with Five New Models in 2027

XPENG’s international business is entering a new phase of growth, with annual overseas vehicle sales on track to surpass 100,000 units for the first time in 2026. In October alone, overseas deliveries reached a record 13,326 vehicles, representing a year-on-year increase of 166%.

XPENG’s global sales and service network now spans 83 countries and regions, with more than 1,300 retail stores worldwide. In Europe, cumulative deliveries have surpassed 10,000 vehicles in each of Denmark, Norway, France and Germany. XPENG also ranks as the best-selling Chinese automotive brand in Europe for battery-electric vehicles priced above €40,000 from January to October 2026, underscoring its strong position in the region’s premium EV market segment.

This momentum is underpinned by growing customer recognition and strong market performance across regions. XPENG ranked first for brand recommendation in the USCALE EV Satisfaction Study across Germany, Austria and Switzerland for two consecutive years, in 2025 and 2026, while the XPENG X9 became the first MPV to win the Luxury category of the German Car of the Year 2027 awards. The X9 also achieved segment-leading sales in several Asia-Pacific markets, while the XPENG GX secured more than 5,000 orders within a month of its introduction across multiple Middle Eastern and African markets.

XPENG’s next wave of international product expansion will begin in December 2026 with the launch of the XPENG L05, a spacious, intelligent five-seat SUV designed for families, in Thailand, its first overseas market. The model will then officially launch in Europe at the Brussels Motor Show in January 2027.

In 2027, XPENG plans to introduce five new vehicle models across key international markets, broadening its product portfolio to address a wider range of customer needs. Among them is the New P7, which will make its international market debut in Europe in the second quarter of 2027. Since its appearance at IAA Mobility 2025 in Munich, the model has attracted interest from European audiences, with its distinctive design earning the prestigious 2026 Red Dot Design Award.

“We aim to more than double our overseas vehicle sales in 2027 compared with 2026,” said Alex, Vice President of XPENG International Business. “But our focus goes beyond sales growth and new vehicle launches. It is about understanding local customer needs, strengthening our local presence and building lasting relationships with customers and partners. These are the foundations for our long-term growth in international markets.”


Alex, Vice President of XPENG International Business, shares XPENG’s global business updates and 2027 international expansion plans at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.

Accelerating the Global Rollout of X-Energy Megawatt Charging

Alongside its global vehicle expansion, XPENG is accelerating the deployment of its X-Energy megawatt charging infrastructure, with plans to expand its network across three continents by the end of 2026. Following the opening of its first X-Energy megawatt charging station in Hong Kong in September 2026, XPENG plans to deploy its second station in Hong Kong, Australia’s first megawatt charging station, and its first two X-Energy stations in Europe, located in Germany and the Netherlands, respectively.

Built on XPENG’s in-house-developed energy storage and ultra-fast charging technology, the X-Energy system can deliver up to 1,000 kW of peak power with a grid connection of no more than 240 kW. By using stored energy to boost charging output, the system reduces pressure on local power grids and facilitates the deployment of megawatt charging infrastructure in densely populated urban areas with limited grid capacity and space, while supporting the second-life use of retired EV batteries.

From Advanced Driver Assistance to Autonomous Mobility

Beyond expanding its vehicle portfolio, XPENG is accelerating the international introduction of its advanced driver-assistance technology. Building on large-scale public test rides at the Paris Motor Show, XPENG became the first Chinese automaker to offer public test rides of advanced urban driver-assistance technology at an overseas retail location, bringing its intelligent driving technology closer to everyday consumers.

Powered by the VLA 2.0 architecture, XPENG’s advanced driver-assistance system, NGP, is undergoing international testing and localisation ahead of a planned overseas rollout in the first half of 2027, subject to local validation, regulatory requirements and market readiness.

XPENG is also extending its Physical AI capabilities into autonomous mobility through YoYo-01, its purpose-built Robotaxi, which is undergoing Level 4 autonomous driving tests. Built on XPENG’s fully in-house-developed technology stack, including its Turing AI chips, VLA 2.0 model and autonomous driving software, YoYo-01 leverages a shared AI technology foundation spanning Level 2 driver assistance and Level 4 autonomous driving.

With a global launch targeted for 2027, XPENG aims to explore international opportunities in Robotaxi services, expanding the application of its AI technologies beyond private vehicles.

As XPENG enters its next phase of global growth, its international strategy is evolving beyond intelligent vehicles to encompass a broader ecosystem of Physical AI technologies. Through AI vehicles, humanoid robots and Robotaxis, XPENG aims to bring the benefits of AI into everyday life for people around the world.

XPENG is a leading global Physical AI company, dedicated to bringing artificial intelligence into the physical world to reshape future mobility and smart living. Through in-house R&D, XPENG has developed a full-stack Physical AI architecture spanning Turing AI chips, world foundation models, and highly integrated software and hardware applications. This unified technology foundation of XPENG powers an expansive product portfolio of smart EVs, robotaxis, and humanoid robots, advancing the deployment of Physical AI at scale.

NexMove, a joint venture between Transportation Management Services and Zeem Solutions, plans to bundle buses, charging, maintenance and operations in a single agreement. It intends to offer a 97% uptime service-level commitment, with certified bus deliveries expected to begin in the first quarter of 2028. The announcement followed VinFast’s September 2026 franchise agreements for three U.S. dealerships in California and Pennsylvania.

Making electric mobility practical for fleets and drivers

For a transit agency, introducing electric buses requires decisions about depot charging, maintenance schedules and daily vehicle availability. NexMove’s proposed service brings these elements together into one agreement. Ahead of certified deliveries, NexMove plans to place demonstration buses at Zeem’s charging depots, where transit agencies and fleet operators can evaluate the vehicles firsthand. The demonstration units are intended for evaluation, with certified vehicles to follow on the planned delivery schedule.

VinFast’s buses combine camera- and radar-based driver assistance, fast charging capabilities, lithium iron phosphate batteries and corrosion protection. The company reported that approximately 2,000 of its electric buses were operating in Vietnam at the time of the announcement. VinFast’s experience in the market spans manufacturing, operations and maintenance, giving it firsthand knowledge of the demands fleet operators face when vehicles are in daily service.

“Bringing VinFast electric buses to the United States marks an important next step in our long-term commitment to this market,” said Brian Finnerty, CEO of VinFast North America.

For households, the questions are more personal: How much will it cost to charge a vehicle each month? Where can it be serviced? What options are available at a price the buyer can afford? The franchise agreements in Redondo Beach and Tustin, California, and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, expand access to sales and after-sales service. The company’s U.S. certified pre-owned program gives buyers another option when weighing the upfront cost of an EV.

In Canada, VinFast offers a 10-year or 200,000-kilometre limited new-vehicle warranty on the VF 8, whichever comes first. Its online energy-cost calculator allows shoppers to compare estimated EV charging costs with the fueling costs of a gasoline vehicle over their expected mileage and ownership period. The comparison gives buyers a clearer picture of how an EV could fit their driving habits and household budget.

Annual EV charging costs can be 50% or more below gasoline fueling costs, depending on electricity rates, whether drivers charge at home or use public stations, driving habits, and vehicle efficiency. Coltura’s Q3 2024 analysis estimated that U.S. EV drivers saved an average of 7.4 cents per mile on fuel. At 1,200 miles a month, that works out to about $90 a month, or nearly $1,100 a year if the same per-mile savings hold.

Why a long-term climate commitment matters as markets change

VinFast announced its transition to all-electric vehicle production at CES in Las Vegas in 2022. Just over two years later, it became Vietnam’s best-selling vehicle brand in 2024, according to Vingroup’s annual report. Its expansion into North America brings a different set of considerations, including where to build out sales and service operations, how to support charging infrastructure and how to help commercial customers integrate electric vehicles into their existing operations.

Incentives, regulations and customer demand can change while a factory upgrade or charging project is still in development. VinFast’s 2040 net-zero goal provides a long-term framework for investments that take years to plan and implement. For example, the timing of an equipment replacement affects when a plant can shift more of its operations to electricity. The source of that electricity then affects the emissions associated with running the equipment. Decisions about materials and suppliers have a similar bearing on emissions across the value chain.

VinFast’s emissions inventory illustrates why those decisions matter as production grows. The company calculated that its emissions exceeded 1.12 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) in its 2022 base year. In a separate scenario, VinFast estimated that emissions could exceed 20 million metric tons of CO₂e if its existing production operations in Vietnam reached their maximum registered capacity, excluding future factories. The estimate illustrates the importance of factoring energy efficiency, electricity sourcing and supplier emissions into plans for higher production.

How the 3E Mission puts the 2040 pledge into practice

VinFast signed The Climate Pledge on August 17, 2022, and announced its participation in September 2022. It was the first Vietnamese enterprise to sign the pledge, an initiative co-founded by Amazon and Global Optimism. The company’s stated goal is to reach net-zero emissions by 2040 across Scopes 1, 2 and 3, covering direct emissions from its operations, indirect emissions from purchased energy, and emissions across its wider value chain. Signatories commit to measuring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions regularly, reducing emissions and neutralizing the remainder.

In January 2025, VinFast’s chairwoman approved the company’s net-zero strategy through 2030, with a view to 2040. The strategy centers on the 3E Mission, which sets out how VinFast plans to change the equipment it uses, reduce the energy it needs and source cleaner power.

  • Electrification. VinFast plans to electrify equipment at company-owned production and business sites by 2030. The roadmap also includes expanding access to charging and developing battery energy storage.
  • Energy Saving. VinFast plans to introduce smart energy monitoring at manufacturing facilities by 2028. Monitoring production lines and major electricity-consuming equipment gives factory teams more detailed information on where energy is used and where operations can be made more efficient.
  • Energy Greening. VinFast aims to use 100% renewable electricity at all its plants by 2040. Its roadmap includes rooftop solar, battery storage to support renewable power use, and work with suppliers on lower-emission materials.

VinFast’s manufacturing complex in Hai Phong offers a practical example of what these priorities translate to on the factory floor. The company reported that upgrades to lighting and compressed-air systems, changes to how production robots operate, and other efficiency measures saved approximately 2.7 million kilowatt-hours of electricity in 2024, equivalent to an estimated 1,782 metric tons of CO₂e.

The company also said it initiated a 30-megawatt-peak rooftop solar project at the site. While the efficiency measures address how much electricity the plant needs, the solar project addresses the source of the electricity.

Against its 2022 baseline, VinFast aims to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 42% and Scope 3 emissions by 29% by 2030. By 2040, the strategy calls for cutting total emissions by at least 85% and neutralizing residual emissions of up to 15% through carbon offsetting mechanisms, which could include carbon credits. As VinFast serves more drivers and fleets, its reported emissions will show how far the company has progressed toward those targets across its operations, purchased energy and value chain.

Key Terms

lithium iron phosphate batteriestechnical
A lithium iron phosphate battery (often called LiFePO4) is a type of rechargeable lithium-ion battery that uses iron phosphate for the cathode material. Compared with other lithium-ion chemistries it typically offers greater thermal stability and longer cycle life but lower energy density, so it is less compact but more durable and safer—like choosing a bulky, long-lasting toolbox over a lighter one that wears out faster. Investors care because this chemistry affects product cost, safety, range and lifespan, and ties to different raw-material and manufacturing supply chains.
scopes 1, 2 and 3technical
Scopes 1, 2 and 3 are categories used to classify an organization’s greenhouse gas emissions. Scope 1 covers emissions from sources it owns or controls, Scope 2 covers emissions from the energy it buys, and Scope 3 covers other indirect emissions across its value chain, such as those from suppliers and the use or disposal of its products.
carbon creditsfinancial
Carbon credits are tradable permits that represent the right to emit a specific amount of greenhouse gases, or the removal of that amount from the atmosphere; think of them like coupons companies buy or sell to balance their pollution. They matter to investors because they create costs or potential revenue streams, affect a company's regulatory compliance and reputation, and form a marketable asset whose price can influence profitability and valuation.

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- X Financial (NYSE: XYF), a leading Chinese fintech platform, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. This press release should be read in conjunction with the Company's Report on Form 6-K for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, which has been furnished to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and is available on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov and on the Company's investor relations website at http://ir.xiaoyinggroup.com.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operational Highlights

  • Total net revenue in Q3 2026 was RMB771.5 million (US$115.1 million), a decrease of 60.7% year-over-year and 22.4% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year decline was mainly attributable to substantially lower loan facilitation volumes, which reduced loan facilitation service revenue and post-origination service revenue, as well as lower financing income.
  • Total loan amount facilitated and originated[1] in Q3 2026 was RMB4.35 billion, down 62.6% quarter-over-quarter and down 87.1% year-over-year.
  • Net loss in Q3 2026 was RMB159.6 million (US$23.8 million), compared with net income of RMB421.2 million a year ago and RMB47.0 million in Q2 2026, primarily reflecting income tax expense of RMB184.6 million and a loss from equity in affiliates, net of tax, of RMB70.9 million, which together exceeded income before income taxes of RMB101.9 million.
  • Delinquency rates for loans 31–60 days past due increased to 2.40% (from 1.73% at the end of Q2 2026 and 1.85% a year ago); loans 91–180 days past due declined to 7.83% (from 9.09% at the end of Q2 2026, though up from 3.52% a year ago). The 31–60 day delinquency rate increased both sequentially and year-over-year, indicating that credit trends deteriorated during the quarter, and the 91–180 day delinquency rate, while lower sequentially, remained materially above the prior-year level. During the quarter, the Company observed an increase in the 31–60 day delinquency rate, which may continue in the near term. The Company believes these trends are consistent with broader industry patterns.

Mr. Kent Li, President of X Financial, commented: "In the third quarter of 2026, we facilitated and originated RMB4.3 billion in loans, a decline of 62.6% from the prior quarter and 87.1% year-over-year. Borrower activity continued to contract, with active borrowers declining to approximately 290,269, down 88.1% from a year ago, while the average loan amount per transaction decreased 5.7% quarter-over-quarter to RMB11,983. The 31–60 day delinquency rate increased to 2.40% from 1.73% in the prior quarter, while the 91–180 day rate eased to 7.83% from 9.09%. The increase in the 31–60 day delinquency rate indicates that credit trends deteriorated during the quarter and may continue in the near term, and both delinquency rates remained above prior-year levels. We believe these trends are consistent with broader industry patterns. We therefore continue to prioritize disciplined underwriting, collection effectiveness, and conservative capital deployment. While the business remains under pressure from lower origination volumes and a challenging credit environment, our focus remains on preserving balance sheet resilience and operating flexibility."

Mr. Frank Fuya Zheng, Chief Financial Officer of X Financial, added: "In the third quarter of 2026, total net revenue was RMB771.5 million, a decrease of 60.7% from the same period last year and 22.4% sequentially. Net loss was RMB159.6 million and non-GAAP adjusted net loss was RMB152.2 million, compared with net income of RMB47.0 million and non-GAAP adjusted net income of RMB165.8 million in the prior quarter. Basic loss per ADS was RMB4.38, and non-GAAP adjusted basic loss per ADS was RMB4.14. Operating margin decreased to 11.8% from 19.6% in the prior quarter and from 18.5% in the same period of 2025. We will continue to manage capital conservatively, maintain cost discipline, and preserve liquidity as we navigate the evolving regulatory and operating environment."

The regulatory environment governing internet-based lending in the People's Republic of China continued to evolve during the third quarter of 2026, with authorities maintaining heightened oversight across the consumer credit business chain. VANCOUVER, British Columbia – TheNewswire – November 26, 2026 - Madoro Metals Corp. (“Madoro” or the “Company”) (TSX VENTURE: MDM; OTC: MSTXF; FSE: A2QQ1X), is pleased to provide a further update regarding the proposed reverse takeover transaction with Narrow River Resources Pty Ltd. (“NRR”) previously announced in the Company’s news release dated February 2, 2026, and as most recently updated in the Company’s news release dated September 29, 2026 (the “Proposed Transaction”).

Madoro and NRR continue to advance the remaining components required under TSX Venture Exchange (“TSXV”) Policy 5.2 – Changes of Business and Reverse Takeovers in connection with the Proposed Transaction. The Company has received comments from the TSXV in connection with its review of the Proposed Transaction. Madoro and NRR, together with their respective advisors, are actively working through those comments and completing the remaining transaction documentation and disclosure materials required to advance the Proposed Transaction.

Subject to completion of the TSXV’s review and receipt of the required TSXV approval, the Company currently anticipates holding the shareholder meeting required to approve the Proposed Transaction during the first quarter of 2027. The meeting date has not yet been fixed and will be announced once the TSXV authorizes Madoro to hold a special meeting in connection with the Proposed Transaction.

Accordingly, the Company has elected to hold its annual meeting of shareholders on December 15, 2026. Shareholders are encouraged to consult the Company’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca for further details.

As previously announced, the Company has entered into a definitive share purchase agreement with 9525-9867 Québec Inc. and NRR in respect of the Proposed Transaction. The parties remain committed to advancing the Proposed Transaction and will provide further updates as appropriate.

 

Considering the revised timing for the Proposed Transaction, the Company and NRR have revised the size and composition of the previously announced concurrent non-brokered private placement (the “Private Placement”), having regard to the anticipated financing requirements of the resulting issuer. The revised terms of the Private Placement are for aggregate gross proceeds of up to C$1,450,000, comprised entirely of hard dollar units (“HD Units”). Under the Private Placement, the Company proposes to issue 29,000,000 HD Units at a price of C$0.05 per HD Unit. There will no longer be any flow-through units offered as part of the Private Placement. Each HD Unit will consist of one common share of the Company (a “Common Share”) and one-half of one common share purchase warrant (each whole warrant, an “HD Warrant”).  Each HD Warrant will entitle the holder to purchase one Common Share at a price of C$0.08 for a period of two (2) years from the Closing. Completion of the Private Placement in connection with the Proposed Transaction will remain subject to TSXV acceptance and all other required regulatory approvals.

 

Completion of the Proposed Transaction remains subject to, among other things, regulatory and shareholder approvals, TSXV acceptance, completion of the Private Placement, finalization and mailing of the Circular, completion of ancillary transaction documentation, and satisfaction of other customary closing conditions.

The March 2025 amendment extended certain deadlines for the Company to complete the required cash payments and expenditure commitments.

 

Under the Amendment Agreement, the Company will pay the vendors a final payment of C$30,000 in cash on or before December 31, 2026 (the “Final Payment”) in exchange for a waiver of all remaining exploration expenditure commitments under the Option Agreement. As a result of this third amendment, and following completion of the Final Payment, the Company shall have completed the Option, thereby acquiring a 100% interest in the First Green Lithium Property. The Amendment Agreement remains subject to the approval of the TSXV.

An electric bus partnership in the U.S. and expanded sales and service options for drivers show how VinFast is putting its electric mobility strategy into practice. The company's published climate roadmap outlines how it plans to reduce emissions as the business grows.

IRVINE, Calif., Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- While some automakers have scaled back their North American EV ambitions, VinFast continues to view electric vehicles as essential to addressing climate change. In the U.S. and Canada, the company is focused on making EVs easier to purchase, charge and service while helping customers understand operating costs. Its broader strategy centers on building a network of vehicles, charging infrastructure and services that can support more drivers and fleets over time.

One of the latest steps came on October 6, 2026, when VinFast announced an initial agreement with NexMove at the APTA TRANSform & EXPO in Chicago to bring its electric buses to U.S. customers. NexMove, a joint venture between Transportation Management Services and Zeem Solutions, plans to bundle buses, charging, maintenance and operations in a single agreement. It intends to offer a 97% uptime service-level commitment, with certified bus deliveries expected to begin in the first quarter of 2028. The announcement followed VinFast's September 2026 franchise agreements for three U.S. dealerships in California and Pennsylvania.

Making electric mobility practical for fleets and drivers

For a transit agency, introducing electric buses requires decisions about depot charging, maintenance schedules and daily vehicle availability. NexMove's proposed service brings these elements together into one agreement. Ahead of certified deliveries, NexMove plans to place demonstration buses at Zeem's charging depots, where transit agencies and fleet operators can evaluate the vehicles firsthand. The demonstration units are intended for evaluation, with certified vehicles to follow on the planned delivery schedule. 

VinFast's buses combine camera- and radar-based driver assistance, fast charging capabilities, lithium iron phosphate batteries and corrosion protection. The company reported that approximately 2,000 of its electric buses were operating in Vietnam at the time of the announcement. VinFast's experience in the market spans manufacturing, operations and maintenance, giving it firsthand knowledge of the demands fleet operators face when vehicles are in daily service. 

"Bringing VinFast electric buses to the United States marks an important next step in our long-term commitment to this market," said Brian Finnerty, CEO of VinFast North America. 

For households, the questions are more personal: How much will it cost to charge a vehicle each month? Where can it be serviced? What options are available at a price the buyer can afford? The franchise agreements in Redondo Beach and Tustin, California, and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, expand access to sales and after-sales service. The company's U.S. certified pre-owned program gives buyers another option when weighing the upfront cost of an EV.

In Canada, VinFast offers a 10-year or 200,000-kilometre limited new-vehicle warranty on the VF 8, whichever comes first. Its online energy-cost calculator allows shoppers to compare estimated EV charging costs with the fueling costs of a gasoline vehicle over their expected mileage and ownership period. The comparison gives buyers a clearer picture of how an EV could fit their driving habits and household budget.

Annual EV charging costs can be 50% or more below gasoline fueling costs, depending on electricity rates, whether drivers charge at home or use public stations, driving habits, and vehicle efficiency. Coltura's Q3 2024 analysis estimated that U.S. EV drivers saved an average of 7.4 cents per mile on fuel. At 1,200 miles a month, that works out to about $90 a month, or nearly $1,100 a year if the same per-mile savings hold.

Why a long-term climate commitment matters as markets change

VinFast announced its transition to all-electric vehicle production at CES in Las Vegas in 2022. Just over two years later, it became Vietnam's best-selling vehicle brand in 2024, according to Vingroup's annual report. Its expansion into North America brings a different set of considerations, including where to build out sales and service operations, how to support charging infrastructure and how to help commercial customers integrate electric vehicles into their existing operations. 

Incentives, regulations and customer demand can change while a factory upgrade or charging project is still in development. VinFast's 2040 net-zero goal provides a long-term framework for investments that take years to plan and implement. For example, the timing of an equipment replacement affects when a plant can shift more of its operations to electricity. The source of that electricity then affects the emissions associated with running the equipment. Decisions about materials and suppliers have a similar bearing on emissions across the value chain. 

VinFast's emissions inventory illustrates why those decisions matter as production grows. The company calculated that its emissions exceeded 1.12 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) in its 2022 base year. In a separate scenario, VinFast estimated that emissions could exceed 20 million metric tons of CO₂e if its existing production operations in Vietnam reached their maximum registered capacity, excluding future factories. The estimate illustrates the importance of factoring energy efficiency, electricity sourcing and supplier emissions into plans for higher production. 

How the 3E Mission puts the 2040 pledge into practice

VinFast signed The Climate Pledge on August 17, 2022, and announced its participation in September 2022. It was the first Vietnamese enterprise to sign the pledge, an initiative co-founded by Amazon and Global Optimism. The company's stated goal is to reach net-zero emissions by 2040 across Scopes 1, 2 and 3, covering direct emissions from its operations, indirect emissions from purchased energy, and emissions across its wider value chain. Signatories commit to measuring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions regularly, reducing emissions and neutralizing the remainder.

In January 2025, VinFast's chairwoman approved the company's net-zero strategy through 2030, with a view to 2040. The strategy centers on the 3E Mission, which sets out how VinFast plans to change the equipment it uses, reduce the energy it needs and source cleaner power. 

  • Electrification. VinFast plans to electrify equipment at company-owned production and business sites by 2030. The roadmap also includes expanding access to charging and developing battery energy storage.
  • Energy Saving. VinFast plans to introduce smart energy monitoring at manufacturing facilities by 2028. Monitoring production lines and major electricity-consuming equipment gives factory teams more detailed information on where energy is used and where operations can be made more efficient.
  • Energy Greening. VinFast aims to use 100% renewable electricity at all its plants by 2040. Its roadmap includes rooftop solar, battery storage to support renewable power use, and work with suppliers on lower-emission materials.

VinFast's manufacturing complex in Hai Phong offers a practical example of what these priorities translate to on the factory floor. The company reported that upgrades to lighting and compressed-air systems, changes to how production robots operate, and other efficiency measures saved approximately 2.7 million kilowatt-hours of electricity in 2024, equivalent to an estimated 1,782 metric tons of CO₂e.

The company also said it initiated a 30-megawatt-peak rooftop solar project at the site. While the efficiency measures address how much electricity the plant needs, the solar project addresses the source of the electricity.

Against its 2022 baseline, VinFast aims to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 42% and Scope 3 emissions by 29% by 2030. By 2040, the strategy calls for cutting total emissions by at least 85% and neutralizing residual emissions of up to 15% through carbon offsetting mechanisms, which could include carbon credits. As VinFast serves more drivers and fleets, its reported emissions will show how far the company has progressed toward those targets across its operations, purchased energy and value chain.

DUBLIN, IE / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Great Western Mining Corporation PLC (AIM:GWMO)(Euronext Growth:8GW)(OTCQB:GWMOF), a strategic minerals exploration and development company, is pleased to provide an update on its Defender Tungsten Project ("Defender" or the "Project") in Mineral County, Nevada, USA, following the identification of a newly discovered adit approximately 400m west of the historical Widowmaker Mine. The Company has named this the Starry Night Mine ("Starry Night") and intends to prioritise sampling work there as part of its next phase of fieldwork in the coming weeks.

Starry Night Mine

Starry Night was identified by the Company's technical team during recent reconnaissance work at Defender and initial field observations, including shortwave ultraviolet ("SWUV") inspection, have identified approximately 50m of scheelite-bearing garnet skarn mineralisation along the adit.

As announced on 7 July 2026, it is theorised that a 3km skarn trend extends from the Defender Mine through the Pine Crow and Widowmaker Mines to the Company's JORC-compliant M2 skarn copper resource. As described in the Company's announcement of 18 August 2026, the Project comprises the historical Widowmaker, Pine Crow, Dough God and Defender tungsten mines, located along a >2km mineralised corridor within the total 3km mineralised trend running from Defender to the M2 resource.

Located west of Widowmaker, Starry Night has the potential to extend the Project's tungsten strike from approximately 2km to approximately 2.4km and lies along the 3km trend linking the Project to the M2 resource 600m away.

The Company intends to prioritise channel sampling at Starry Night and further updates will reported as results are received.

Figure 1: Location of the Starry Night Mine and extension of identified strike towards the M2 copper resource in the west.

Drill Assays and Maiden Mineral Resource Estimate

As announced on 23 September 2026, the Company completed a 23-hole reverse circulation drilling programme for approximately 8,500 ft (2,590 m) at Defender, with all samples dispatched to American Assay in Reno, Nevada. Assay results were expected in Q4 2026 however processing has since been delayed by laboratory capacity constraints affecting the region, and results are still outstanding.

Addison Mining Services ("Addison"), the independent Competent Person engaged to prepare the maiden JORC Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE"), has been closely involved in the programme to date, including supervising the drilling. The Company therefore expects to be well positioned to progress the MRE promptly once assays are received.

Ed Loye, CEO of Great Western, commented: "Identifying Starry Night, a historical mine adit west of Widowmaker, is another very encouraging development for Defender. It has the potential to extend our tungsten strike to around 2.4km and adds a further valuable data point along the trend towards our M2 resource. We intend to prioritise sampling at Starry Night, and the team are keen to get on site as soon as possible, whilst noting winter weather conditions.

"The delay to our drill assays is frustrating, but not unique to Great Western. Laboratory capacity constraints are affecting the industry across the region and are a symptom of the current buoyant mining landscape in Nevada. Addison has been closely involved since before drilling began, which puts us in a good position to move quickly once results are received. The assays and maiden resource are expected to give us a much fuller picture of our opportunity at Defender as we look towards mine development."
